svg.title: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate: Lizard receives the options a developer types after task lizard --
svg.text: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate
Scenario: Lizard receives the options a developer types after task lizard --

g.text: Given a generated project holds a function with four paths through it
A project generated from the toolbox, with one file of the developer's own: src/shipping.py.
Its function shipping_cost has two if lines and one elif, so there are four paths through it.
Lizard counts those paths as the function's cyclomatic complexity, CCN in its tables.
When the developer runs task lizard, the function stays under Lizard's default limit of 15
The developer runs Lizard through the toolbox. TASK_LIZARD_PATH_TO_ANALYSE=src points it at the developer's own code.
Task first prints the script it runs, and that script's last line starts Lizard.
The table gives shipping_cost a CCN of 4. Lizard answers "No thresholds exceeded (cyclomatic_complexity > 15 ...)": 15
is its default limit. The run ends with exit code 0. Versions show as <version>: they move with each update.
Then with --CCN 3 after the two dashes, Lizard flags the function and the run fails
The same command with --CCN 3 after the two dashes. The last line of the script now ends with --CCN 3: Task hands the
Lizard lists shipping_cost under "Warnings (cyclomatic_complexity > 3 ...)" and fails, so Task stops with exit code 201,
the code it gives a failed command.
